value.title: Round rules as of 21 Nov: 450k line, FYI-only outputs, build queue, rollouts

sections.name: body
sections.value:
Round rules as of 21 Nov (prime far-jackal, after the 18 Nov revive). Supersedes the 600k line and the start-here state line.
- Compact any pij-fleet seat from about 450k, at its next idle boundary, fire and forget: pij send <seat> --command compact. A working seat over 450k can be sent it at once, because it's held until the turn ends. Never compact the prime, Jordan's panes (takin, macaw, bright-jay) or other projects' seats. Compact yourself with pij compact-self at 450k.
- Seats with ctx "?" in the digest: read the pane footer (Copilot NNNk/1.0M; OMP NN.N%/1M or %/400K for GPT).
- Wake the PM or prime with a normal send when a reviewer's or worker's output reached it only as an FYI and the producer is idle (e.g. "[pij output] ... wrote a note for role reviewer on pr:N"). Status notes and acks stay as FYIs.
- Declared "blocked" or "waiting" reviewers are usually holding reviewer/<pr> for round 2 or merge, which is intended. Check the pane's last line before flagging.
- Seats working with no model call for 20-60 min are usually queued on just shared-build (one heavy build at a time; its --timeout is minutes). Check with ps for shared-build.sh sleeping on sleep 20. A test binary at 0% CPU far past its normal time is hung: give the pid to the seat's parent, and don't kill it yourself.
- Stale-extension after a daemon bounce: Copilot needs a rollout only if the Copilot tree changes; OMP only if the +part after the base tree changes. The prime decides each rollout.
- Launch-rate attribution: import harness/scripts/spawn-rate.py, poll its libproc pids()/info() for 20 s, and walk each new pid's ppid to a tmux pane_pid and seat. ps sampling misses most short-lived launches.
